Class Refactor

java.lang.Object
uno.anahata.asi.agi.tool.ToolContext
uno.anahata.asi.agi.tool.AnahataToolkit
uno.anahata.asi.intellij.tools.ide.Refactor
All Implemented Interfaces:
ContextProvider, PropertyChangeSource, Rebindable
public class Refactor extends AnahataToolkit
Programmatic Java refactoring for IntelliJ IDEA: project-wide rename, safe delete, and find-usages.

This is the IntelliJ port of the NetBeans Refactor toolkit. Where NetBeans drives org.netbeans.modules.refactoring.api.*, IntelliJ uses RefactoringFactory (rename / safe-delete) and ReferencesSearch (find-usages), move and copy (class and static members), pull-up/push-down, inline-method, change-signature, and extract superclass/interface — the full NetBeans Refactor surface. Refactorings run non-interactively (no preview dialog) on the EDT and update every reference across all open projects. The processor-based operations use java-impl-refactorings; copy is a PSI file-copy + package fix-up + optional rename.

Author:
anahata

    • copyClass

      public String copyClass(String filePath, String targetPackage, String newName) throws AgiToolException
      Copies a top-level class to another package, optionally renaming it.

      The source file is copied into the target package directory (created under the source's source root if it does not exist), the copy's package declaration is rewritten, and — if a new name is given — the copied class (and its constructors and file) are renamed. The original is left untouched.

      Parameters:
      filePath - the absolute path of the .java file to copy.
      targetPackage - the destination package FQN.
      newName - the new class name, or null to keep the original.
      Returns:
      a confirmation message.
      Throws:
      AgiToolException - if the source, target package, or copy operation fails.

    • resolveOrCreateTargetDir

      private com.intellij.psi.PsiDirectory resolveOrCreateTargetDir(com.intellij.openapi.project.Project project, com.intellij.psi.PsiClass source, String targetPackage)
      Resolves the target package's directory, preferring one under the source's own source root, and creating the package directory chain if it does not yet exist. Must be called inside a write action (it may create directories).
      Parameters:
      project - the host project.
      source - the class being copied (used to locate the source root).
      targetPackage - the destination package FQN.
      Returns:
      the target directory, or null if it cannot be resolved or created.
